item.title: Palo Alto to create retail zones on El Camino amid housing influx
item.description: After spending the past two years trying to supercharge residential development along El Camino Real, Palo Alto’s elected leaders are preparing to tackle next week one of the possible pitfalls of the city’s housing strategy: the potential loss of retail along the eclectic commercial artery. item.title: Silicon Valley restaurants share recipes for Super Bowl snacking
item.description: The Bay is abuzz with watch parties and events for the Super Bowl at Levi’s Stadium Feb. 8. But for those viewing the big game from home or at a friends’ place, snack preparation is likely on the calendar. To make sure your Super Bowl Sunday is entertaining and delicious, we’ve rounded up recipes from local restaurants. item.title: San Francisco denies Palo Alto appeal of airport enhancement plan
item.description: San Francisco will proceed with its airline development plan for SFO after rejecting an appeal on Tuesday from the city of Palo Alto, which argued that issues like noise and air quality were not appropriately accounted for during the environmental review process. The post San Francisco denies Palo Alto appeal of airport enhancement plan appeared first on Palo Alto Online.

item.title: From Farm to Fed chair: Kevin Warsh prepares for confirmation
item.description: When Kevin Warsh won the race become chair of the Student Senate at Stanford University in 1991, he vowed that he would not be “manipulated by political parties.” With Warsh now is poised to assume another role as chair – this time at the Federal Reserve — many are wondering if this stance still applies.
